create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl (string) as alternative.

saml.description: Access tokens, especially opaque tokens, are bearer credentials intended to be presented multiple times until expiry or revocation.
saml.note: Do not report repeated successful use of the same access token as replay unless the test targets a one-time SAML assertion or other explicit single-use proof.

saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML authentication flows.
saml.note: IdP-initiated attempts failing are expected and should not be treated as flow-coherence bugs.

saml.description: SAML endpoint responses can use HTTP 200 even when the SAML operation failed, with failure encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message.
saml.note: HTTP status alone is not a reliable oracle for SAML success/failure.

saml.description: SAML SSO endpoint reports protocol errors inside the SAML response while still using HTTP 200.
saml.note: Do not infer successful authentication from HTTP status alone.

saml.description: When requested_token_type is id_token in token exchange, the returned ID token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A.
saml.note: This odd response shape is RFC-driven and should not be mistaken for token confusion.

saml.description: Token introspection only reports active=true when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
saml.note: Inactive introspection from a non-audience client is expected and not proof the token is invalid.

saml.description: ZITADEL issues opaque access tokens by default rather than JWTs.
saml.note: Failure to locally decode access_token is expected and not a bug.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. The fuzzer MUST initiate the service-provider flow first and obtain a SAML request/intent before attempting saml_login; IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid on this platform.

For SAML broker tests against ZITADEL as service provider, user creation in Login V2 can fail unless required user fields are mapped from upstream SAML attributes via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. The fuzzer MUST ensure upstream assertions provide required attributes (email, first/given name, last/family name, identifier) or preconfigure equivalent response manipulation; otherwise login failure is setup-related, not a security oracle.

SAML endpoint errors may be returned with HTTP 200 and encoded only in the SAML StatusCode/message. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 alone as successful SAML authentication when evaluating SAML protocol outcomes.

When testing I2 freshness on OIDC id_tokens, nonce is only mandatory for implicit flow. A missing nonce in code flow is not by itself a violation from these docs; nonce-based replay tests MUST target implicit-flow or explicit RP validation behavior, not plain authorization-code requests without nonce.

For I2 expired/future JWT timing tests against /oauth/v2/token JWT profile or private_key_jwt auth, the JWT iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Failures outside those bounds are expected setup failures, not evidence of exp/nbf enforcement bugs.

For I5 token exchange audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. If the fuzzer requests a new audience not already present, rejection is by design and MUST NOT be flagged as a vulnerability.

For I5 token exchange scope escalation tests, ZITADEL allows scope to differ from supplied tokens but validates it. The oracle MUST inspect the returned scope and claims, not just token issuance. A successful exchange with reduced/validated scope is by design; only issuance of claims beyond validated scope is suspicious.

For I5 token exchange subject-token audience tests, introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST use a client in the token audience for control introspection; otherwise inactive/401 results are expected and not evidence of invalid token handling.

For I2 replay_same_token, opaque/JWT access tokens are designed for repeated bearer use until expiry or revocation. The fuzzer MUST NOT flag simple repeated use of the same access token as a replay vulnerability. Replay-focused tests should target SAML assertions or explicit one-time semantics instead.

For I2 SAML replay tests, ZITADEL documentation states best practice to use historical cache and reject duplicate IDs, but the provided docs do not expose a direct ACS endpoint for external forged assertions in broker mode. The fuzzer MUST distinguish between ZITADEL acting as SAML IdP (/saml/v2/SSO) and ZITADEL acting as brokered SP via custom login/SAML request finalization; do not send forged SAMLResponse directly to /saml/v2/SSO because that endpoint is IdP-side, not ACS.

If organization-specific login settings override defaults, the authorization request MUST include the organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise the wrong IdP/login policy may be used and cross-tenant or MFA tests can produce false positives.

The token exchange parameter resource is currently not supported. Supplying it will always result in invalid_target and MUST NOT be used in security test sequences except to confirm documented rejection.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. For SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST initiate the flow through /saml/v2/SSO and preserve request state; IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid against this platform.

The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even on SAML protocol errors; failure is conveyed inside the SAML StatusCode/message, not the HTTP status. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 from /saml/v2/SSO as successful authentication by itself.

For SAML-brokered logins, ZITADEL completes authentication through its OIDC flow. A valid end-to-end test SHOULD use /oauth/v2/authorize followed by /oauth/v2/token and then /oidc/v1/userinfo to observe the granted identity, rather than assuming the SAML endpoint itself yields a bearer session token.

When testing I2 nonce-related OIDC callback behavior after SAML brokering, include nonce in the authorization request whenever the flow expects ID token validation. ZITADEL documents nonce as replay mitigation and says it MUST be provided for implicit flow; missing nonce can make results ambiguous.

For I2 expired/future JWT control tests on /oauth/v2/token JWT profile grant, the JWT iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and aud MUST include the ZITADEL issuing domain. Use control claims like iat={{now_epoch}}, exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. Otherwise rejection may be due to malformed client assertion setup rather than freshness enforcement.

Token introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST introspect with the intended audience client; inactive/401 results from another client can be by design and are not proof of token invalidity.

For token exchange audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. If audience is outside that union, rejection is by design. The fuzzer MUST seed subject/actor tokens with the target audience before testing whether ZITADEL improperly broadens audience.

For token exchange scope-escalation tests, ZITADEL allows scope to differ from supplied tokens but validates the input and may return a different final scope. The oracle MUST compare the returned scope and claims, not just whether the request was accepted.
The token exchange resource parameter is not supported and always results in invalid_target. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource to model audience tests on ZITADEL; use audience instead.

When requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that returned access_token field as a bearer API credential.

Refresh tokens are not allowed as subject_token or actor_token in token exchange. Tests that submit refresh tokens to RFC 8693 on ZITADEL will fail by design and should not be interpreted as security enforcement beyond documented behavior.

ZITADEL currently rejects expired ID tokens even when used as subject_token in token exchange. For token-exchange freshness tests, use a valid control ID token first; otherwise failure may reflect documented token-type handling rather than a replay/freshness defense specific to the attack.

For impersonation tests, actor_token is optional syntactically but required for ZITADEL's user_id and self-signed JWT subject_token impersonation modes, and the actor must hold impersonation permissions. The fuzzer MUST provision impersonation roles before testing cross-subject token exchange.

For multi-tenant or organization-scoped SAML/OIDC tests, if organization-specific settings override defaults, the authorization request MUST include the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may apply default instance settings and route to the wrong IdP configuration.

Reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces that the user is a member of the selected organization. Unknown organizations fail, and omission changes tenant selection semantics. The fuzzer MUST use the correct org scope when testing tenant isolation or cross-org identity behavior.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST initiate the brokered login through the application/OIDC authorization flow first and only then submit the SAMLResponse to the callback. IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid on this platform.

For SAML broker tests, saml_login MUST be preceded by start_oidc_auth because ZITADEL acts as the broker and completes login through OIDC after the external SAML step. A standalone SAMLResponse submission without an existing auth request / intent will not represent a valid flow.

SAML SSO endpoint errors are returned with HTTP 200 and encoded inside the SAML StatusCode/message. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 from SAML-facing steps as success by itself; success/failure must be determined by whether the downstream OIDC code/token flow completes.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, ZITADEL documentation states SAML assertions/responses should be validated and signed trust is established via exchanged metadata/certificates. The fuzzer MUST configure a SAML provider with metadata/certificate trust first; acceptance of attacker-signed assertions would only be meaningful after a trusted provider exists.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay, use TWO saml_login events within the SAME configured provider context and same broker flow shape. Because ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML, each replay attempt must still be tied to a valid initiated flow; otherwise rejection may be due to missing request correlation rather than replay protection.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, include a CONTROL brokered login first that uses the same provider and flow without expired_assertion=true. Without a successful control, a failed expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken SAML provider setup or missing required user-mapping actions.

Login V2 SAML brokering may require Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent to map returned SAML attributes into required ZITADEL user fields. If required fields are not populated, user creation fails. The fuzzer MUST ensure the upstream SAML assertion provides required attributes or preconfigure the mapping action; otherwise login failures are setup failures, not security rejections.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, ZITADEL may create or link users based on external IdP information and configured linking/creation behavior. The fuzzer MUST control whether account creation/linking is allowed when interpreting identity merges; otherwise a merge may be by-design account linking rather than principal-collision.

If organization-specific login settings override default settings, the authorization request MUST include the reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise the wrong IdP/login policy may be selected and SAML tests may exercise default settings instead of the intended tenant configuration.

Reserved audience scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud add project IDs to the access-token audience. For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly control these scopes because ZITADEL can legitimately widen audience based on requested reserved scopes.

Token exchange audience is restrictive: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience / ignore_audience tests, the fuzzer must first mint subject/actor tokens with known audiences and then request an audience outside that combined set; otherwise acceptance/rejection is uninterpretable.

Token exchange scope semantics are not simple intersection. ZITADEL documentation says requested scope can be entirely different from supplied tokens and is then validated by ZITADEL. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the returned scope and claims against upstream authorization and broker policy rather than assuming omitted scope means denial. Include a control exchange with unchanged scope.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. For freshness tests involving token exchange with id_token subject tokens, rejection of expired subject_token is by design and not evidence of broader replay tracking.
The resource parameter in token exchange is currently not supported and always results in invalid_target. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource to model audience tests on ZITADEL; use audience instead.

For client_assertion / private_key_jwt authentication to token or introspection endpoints, JWT aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use template times such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for controls. Failures outside these bounds are setup failures, not target invariant violations.

For I2 freshness tests against OIDC/OAuth tokens, include a control login using a valid token/code flow alongside the attack case. ZITADEL returns 401 for invalid or expired userinfo tokens and invalid_grant/invalid_client style token errors; without a control, failures cannot be distinguished from bad client authentication or bad redirect_uri/client setup.

Introspection returns active=true only if the token is active AND the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection as a client that is in the token audience; otherwise active=false is expected and not evidence of token invalidity.

ZITADEL uses opaque access tokens by default. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume access_token is locally parseable JWT unless the application/token exchange explicitly requested JWT token type. Use introspection or userinfo for verification when opaque tokens are returned.

The authorization endpoint requires redirect_uri to match exactly a preregistered URI. For brokered SAML tests that start with OIDC, any mismatch causes authorization failure unrelated to SAML security behavior.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths (e.g., 'zitadel.idp.v2.IdentityProviderService/...'). For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy. Both are needed before IdP login works.
